solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Shortly wake occasional visitor (5)

indicators.note: cut short: the phrase loses its last letter

blocks.note: to wake is to come to, regain consciousness; 'Shortly' docks the final O of that two-word phrase

annotation.surface: Someone is told to wake briefly for a visitor who rarely calls.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wake' is a verb here, and the two-word phrase COME TO is what gets docked, not a single word.
annotation.definitionFit: A comet returns to our skies only now and then, a visitor seen at long intervals.

entries.clue: Supply teacher welcomes popular girl (9)

indicators.note: supple, loosely: TEACHER is bent into a new order
the rearranged teacher takes IN inside

annotation.surface: A school takes on a supply teacher who proves a hit with the pupils.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply teacher' reads as one familiar phrase, a stand-in at school; split it, and 'Supply' is an adverb meaning in a supple, bendy way.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the answer is one particular girl's name, so 'girl' stands for any first name a girl might have.

entries.clue: Frontier family of sisters advance steadily (5)

blocks.note: an old word for a border territory, as in the Welsh borderlands
Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women share this surname
to walk on in step, as soldiers do

annotation.surface: Pioneer sisters push steadily westward across the frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions, not two: a border territory, Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy March of Little Women, and to advance in step.
annotation.definitionFit: A march is a borderland, the frontier between two realms.

entries.clue: Dessert: for a change, it’s a rum one (8)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone at dinner orders something different and remarks that the pudding is a strange one.
annotation.walkthrough: A rum one is British for an odd one, which is the surface; but rum really is in tiramisu, a nice touch.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

entries.clue: Fitting tee perhaps something that really doesn’t fit (6,3)

blocks.note: a golf tee is a small peg

annotation.surface: A golfer is fitted with a tee that does not suit at all.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue turns on fit: 'Fitting' is in the wordplay, 'doesn't fit' in the definition, from the saying about a square peg in a round hole.
annotation.definitionFit: A square peg in a round hole is someone or something unsuited to its place.

entries.clue: Small shed is inaccessible (4)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A little garden shed that cannot be got into.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small shed' reads as one item; it is two, S and HUT.
annotation.definitionFit: Something shut, closed up, cannot be entered.

entries.clue: Endlessly stressed over new clothes not to be seen (10)

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter
in a down clue, the first part sits above N

blocks.note: stressed = UNDERLINED, minus its final D

annotation.surface: Someone fretting without end over new clothes that nobody will see.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stressed' means emphasised, as by underlining, not anxious.
annotation.definitionFit: Underlinen is underwear, the linen worn beneath clothes and not meant to be seen.

entries.clue: Seriously damage a volume in foul temper (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places the book, a and volume, within the temper, so those letters sit inside the word for it

annotation.surface: Someone in a foul temper does real harm to a book.
annotation.walkthrough: A and V sit inside RAGE: R-A-V-AGE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: armies and storms ravage a land, leaving it wrecked, which is damage of the serious kind.

entries.clue: State supports case for particularly burning desire (9)

indicators.note: the outside of the word, its first and last letters
in a down clue, the state sits beneath PY

blocks.note: Romania is a country, a state

annotation.surface: A nation backs a case built on a particularly passionate desire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' is a cliché for longing, but here it is literal: an urge to set fires.
annotation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsive urge to start fires, a desire for burning.

entries.clue: With difficulty pick up area in depression (5)

indicators.note: 'in' puts the area in the depression, so its letter lies inside the word for the hollow

blocks.note: a glen is a valley, a depression in land

annotation.surface: Someone struggles to lift a patch of ground in a hollow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is a dip in the landscape, not low spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather bit by bit and laboriously, as gleaners pick up leftover grain.

entries.clue: Face about to go plump (4,5)

blocks.note: a go = a turn, as in a game

annotation.surface: A face is about to become chubby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face' reads as a noun and 'about to' as soon; together 'Face about' is the military command to turn, and 'to' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'about face' is the drill order to reverse direction, so facing about is the same about-turn.

entries.clue: Say priest backed limit (5)

indicators.note: the pair is read backwards

annotation.surface: A priest, for instance, supported a limit.
annotation.walkthrough: EGREV reads backwards as VERGE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the grass strip at a road's edge marks its limit, and being on the brink of something is the same edge.

entries.clue: Dig out Introduction to Ethics by philosopher (6)

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: by = times, the multiplication sign X

annotation.surface: A student is told to hunt out a philosopher's introductory ethics text.
annotation.walkthrough: The italic book title makes 'by' look like authorship; it is X, as in 3 by 4.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin for out of the earth: bodies are exhumed, dug out of graves, and old ideas can be too.

entries.clue: Totter round ring, following daughter as guide (8)

indicators.note: 'round' means surrounding, so the scrap man's letters wrap around the ring
'following' means coming after, so the whole group is placed behind the daughter's letter

blocks.note: a totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man, a ragman

annotation.surface: Someone staggers around a ring behind a daughter who shows the way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Totter' looks like a verb, to wobble; it is a noun, a scrap collector who goes 'totting'. RAG-O-MAN after D.
annotation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic- or Turkish-speaking countries.

entries.clue: Loosely two GIs in turn hatching a plot (10)

indicators.note: the letters are held loosely, free to rearrange

annotation.surface: Two American soldiers take turns, casually, plotting something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two GIs' is not TWO plus GIS but GI written twice.
annotation.definitionFit: Intriguing means scheming, plotting secretly.

entries.clue: Innate bias spread when away in Rome (2,8)

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and reset

annotation.surface: An inbuilt prejudice spreads among travellers in Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Rome' signals Latin: the answer is the Latin phrase for when away.
annotation.definitionFit: In absentia is Latin for in one's absence, that is, when away.

entries.clue: Very delicate song Yankee repeated: loudly joining in (4-5)

indicators.note: 'repeated' means done again, so the song-and-Yankee pair is written a second time
F goes between the two copies

blocks.note: Yankee = Y in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A fragile song is played again with a Yankee crowd noisily singing along.
annotation.walkthrough: AIRY twice, with F between.
annotation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy means delicate, light and insubstantial.

entries.clue: Ruin party at country club? (4)

blocks.note: the United Nations, a club of countries

annotation.surface: A party held at a golf club spells disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'country club' as a pun: not a golf club but the club whose members are countries.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary sense: in old tragedies a villain is 'undone', brought to ruin, the verb that carries the same downfall.

entries.clue: Expenditure for departures? (9)

blocks.note: money spent, in the British household-budget word

annotation.surface: Money spent on people leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'outgoings' for departures is a whimsical literal reading of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Outgoings is a British word for expenditure, money going out.

entries.clue: Economise on protection for soldiers (8)

annotation.surface: Cutting costs on soldiers' protective kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Economise on' looks like one phrasal verb; 'on' is the start of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut back spending.

entries.clue: Noble type of king lacking protection (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters, which protect the rest, are dropped

blocks.note: a pearly king is a London costermonger dressed in pearl buttons
PEARLY minus its outer letters P and Y

annotation.surface: A nobleman is a kind of king with no bodyguard.
annotation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London charity figures in pearl-button suits; the P and Y around EARL are its protective shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the rank sits between viscount and marquess in the British peerage, making its holder a noble.

entries.clue: I am wrong about part of Middle East being unimportant (10)

indicators.note: 'about' as in about-turn: the word for being wrong faces the other way

blocks.note: to err is to be wrong
the Levant, the eastern Mediterranean lands

annotation.surface: Someone admits their mistake about a region, deciding it matters little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I am wrong' reads as one confession; I stays, and ERR turns to RRE.
annotation.definitionFit: Irrelevant means beside the point, unimportant.

entries.clue: Scamp puts on British accent (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, ROGUE is put under B

annotation.surface: A rascal fakes a British accent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puts on' suggests faking an accent; it places ROGUE beneath B.
annotation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish.

entries.clue: Tolerate leaving Europe initially, then get on and vote (8)

indicators.note: a letter goes out of the word
the first E is the one that goes

blocks.note: SUFFER (tolerate) with its first E (Europe) removed
to get on is to grow old, age

annotation.surface: Put up with the exit from Europe, then move on and cast a ballot.
annotation.walkthrough: The Brexit surface hides the mechanics: SUFFER loses its first E, then AGE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means the franchise, the right to cast a vote, and in older use a single vote itself.

entries.clue: Dish from South America and Hawaii (5)

blocks.note: HI is the postal code for Hawaii

annotation.surface: A dish whose origins lie in South America and Hawaii.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South America' reads as one continent; it is S and US.
annotation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with fish.

entries.clue: Power nap over quickly (6)

annotation.surface: A power nap is done and dusted fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power nap' is a stock phrase that must be split: P and REST.
annotation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical direction meaning quickly.

entries.clue: Wise man eating starter of delicious meal to celebrate special occasion (5)

indicators.note: 'eating' means taking in, so the wise man's letters swallow the starter
the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: a seer is a sage, a wise man

annotation.surface: A sage tucks into a tasty starter at a celebratory dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's starter is a first course; the wordplay's is a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The Seder is the ritual Jewish meal that celebrates Passover.

entries.clue: Is sorry about picking up the last trick (4)

indicators.note: the final letter of RUES is lifted one place up the down entry

blocks.note: to rue is to be sorry

annotation.surface: Someone regrets picking up the final card in a hand of bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: The card-game surface makes 'the last trick' one phrase; 'the last' is the final S of RUES, moved up past E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stratagem meant to deceive, the sort of trick used to throw someone off the scent.

entries.clue: Wife comes in to do vocals for big-band music (5)

indicators.note: 'comes in' means enters, so the wife's letter steps inside the singing

blocks.note: to do vocals is to sing

annotation.surface: A bandleader's wife steps up to sing with the orchestra.
annotation.walkthrough: W inside SING.
annotation.definitionFit: A genre named for what it plays: the jazz of Goodman and Ellington's 1930s-40s big bands, with its lilting rhythm.

entries.clue: Big herbivore once seen in Antigua? No donkey (9)

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A tourist asks whether a large plant-eater lives in Antigua, and is told no, not a donkey.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No' break the surface into a dialogue, which hides the run of letters across it.
annotation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, a herbivore of long ago.

entries.clue: Historian missing first by some distance in elite institutions (3,6)

indicators.note: 'missing' means lacking, and what is lacking is the first letter
'by' in its sense of beside: the distance is placed next to the shortened historian

blocks.note: Livy, the Roman historian, without his L
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

annotation.surface: A historian falls well short of the top in elite colleges.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By some distance' reads as by a wide margin, and 'missing first' as coming second; the historian is Livy, the Roman who wrote a history of Rome.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of elite old universities in the north-eastern US.

entries.clue: Hard men lead American power in Egypt (5)

indicators.note: H and OR go in front of US

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: Tough men head an American power bloc in Egypt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power' is a deity, not a nation: Horus was a falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt.
annotation.definitionFit: Horus was an ancient Egyptian god, a divine power.
